text:
amanda: heads-up — ran a long-context perf sweep on canary and saw KV cache residency drop sharply around 28–32s for sessions with repeated prefix reuse. baseline CPU stable, but token latency tail climbs. logs + short trace below. any ideas? :thinking:

josh: can you paste the exact command and the log snippet? is this for the new key derivation change we merged last week?

amanda: repro command:
```
./run_inference --model rwinf-7b-q --seq 4096 --session-id session_42 --warm-prefix "user:order_history" --rate 250
```
log excerpt:
```
[00:00:28.998] kv-residency: keys_active=8743 keys_evicted=1232 shard=3 reason=age
[00:00:29.002] kv-mem: total=3.1G resident=2.7G frag=14% growth=+22MB
[00:00:29.129] request 0x7fbf: prefix-hit=false fallback=true
```
looks like eviction batches kick in and then we start missing prefixes.

sanjay: hmm. two possibilities: 1) our session key is too granular after the last patch (we add dynamic metadata that varies each request) so prefix keys don't coalesce; 2) eviction policy (segmented LRU) biases against mid-hot prefixes. i lean toward key-sanitization bug. can you dump the raw cache keys for one session?

amanda: got a dump for session_42 (redacted):
```
pk:sha256:user:order_history:prompt_v1:seg=3:ctxid=0x1a2b
pk:sha256:user:order_history:prompt_v1:seg=7:ctxid=0x8f00
pk:sha256:user:order_history:prompt_v1:seg=3:ctxid=0x2c33
pk:sha256:user:order_history:prompt_v1:seg=3:ctxid=0x1a2b:nonce=0x101
```
notice the extra `nonce` and ctxid variance — that's probably fragmenting. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:

josh: yep that nonce looks new. which PR added that field? iirc we intended it only for ephemeral tool-calls. if it leaks into normal prefix keying, we multiply unique keys and force eviction.

sanjay: also check our coalescing: we currently coalesce only on exact prefix hash. we could add a normalization pass that strips ephemeral fields before hashing. tradeoff: we lose ability to distinguish intentionally different contexts. i'd add a feature-flagged normalizer and run A/B.

maria: agree with a phased approach. suggestion: A/B with feature flag "prefix_normalizer" toggled for 10% of canaries. metrics to watch: prefix_hit_rate, per-token-latency_p95, kv_evictions/s, mem_resident, and correctness eval on a small prompt set.

perf-bot: automated-metrics: on canary-without-normalizer (24h): prefix_hit_rate=0.62 avg_latency=28ms p95=112ms kv_evictions=1800/h mem_resident=2.9G
perf-bot: automated-metrics: on canary-with-normalizer (24h): prefix_hit_rate=0.86 avg_latency=24ms p95=78ms kv_evictions=420/h mem_resident=2.65G

amanda: those perf-bot numbers look convincing. any gotchas for rollout? what about sessions that intentionally rely on per-request salt?

sanjay: we should keep an allowlist for endpoints that need full-key fidelity (tooling, multimodal calls). implement normalizer to strip only keys matching regex `nonce|ephemeral_id|runtime_ts` when present. leave rest intact. also add a fuzz-test that ensures no correctness regressions for 500 eval prompts.

maria: rollout plan draft:
- stage 1: internal canary (10%) with normalizer, monitor 48h
- stage 2: extend to 50% and run eval regression suite (500 prompts)
- stage 3: 100% if no regressions and p95 improved
config snippet to enable (console flag):
```
services.runtime.kv.prefix_normalizer: true
services.runtime.kv.normalizer_allowlist: ["tools.*", "multimodal.*"]
```

infra-bot: can schedule the feature-flag rollout. note: need DB migration window for the normalizer metadata table (if we track normalization stats). propose maintenance window 02:00 UTC.

amanda: sounds good. i'll open the PR to add the normalizer + unit tests + perf harness. will capture per-session key cardinality metric and a new gauge `kv.fragmentation_ratio`. :thumbsup:

josh: thanks — please ping when PR is up, i'll review quickly. also add a quick shell script to reproduce the fragmentation locally.

amanda: will do. tagging @sanjay for design review and @maria for rollout approval. :eyes:
